subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw change the default SSRF DNS-answer rule for web_fetch from fail on any blocked resolved address to filter blocked candidates and proceed when at least one allowed address remains?
rationale: The code repair is narrow, but the default controls outbound request safety under polluted or hostile DNS answers, so automation should not choose the SSRF boundary without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Filter every blocked resolved address out of the pinned pool, reject only when no allowed address remains, and add mixed-allowed plus all-blocked regression coverage.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat any blocked DNS answer as intentional hard failure and document trusted proxy or fake-IP policy settings as the supported workaround.

options.title: Make the behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for DNS-polluted environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Filter every blocked resolved address out of the pinned pool, reject only when no allowed address remains, and add mixed-allowed plus all-blocked regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest visible history on the SSRF host/IP and IPv6 special-use security boundary.
